# SESAME

> SESAME is Wayne State's sign-in library for PHP. It checks who someone is through CAS, OpenID Connect, an OAuth2 token or the Drawbridge gateway, and hands your app a verified identity. Your app keeps its own session. It works in raw PHP, Laravel with Blade, and Laravel with Inertia and Vue.

**The way in. One lock, any key.** Single Entry, Sessions App-Managed Everywhere: keys cut while you wait, and no
key ever gets to keep the door.

Checks: `composer ci` (the same command runs on GitLab and GitHub). Both pipelines run the same five checks (manifest, tests, Pint, PHPStan, audit), so a green build means the same thing on both sides.

Our CI is the same script on both sides, so when it fails, nobody gets to blame the other platform.

SESAME is Wayne State's protocol-neutral auth library. It returns a verified
identity and leaves the session to the app: every driver ends in the same
place, the app's `findOrImportUser(Identity)`, and the protocol never holds
the session. Switching driver is a config change with no code change. Open
sesame.

Front page: [`site/index.html`](https://github.com/waynestate/sesame/blob/HEAD/site/index.html), a static page you can open in a browser or serve from `site/`.
On Citadel it is served by the raw-PHP deploy layer in [`deploy/`](https://github.com/waynestate/sesame/blob/HEAD/deploy/): a Squire kit whose front controller serves `site/` behind HELMET's security headers. For local development, keep serving `site/` directly.

Documentation: the opening of this README is the [Overview](https://github.com/waynestate/sesame/blob/HEAD/site/docs/index.html) page of the docs site. Squire's docs builder renders [`docs/`](https://github.com/waynestate/sesame/blob/HEAD/docs/) into [`site/docs/`](https://github.com/waynestate/sesame/blob/HEAD/site/docs/index.html); `composer docs` rebuilds it, and `composer docs:check` fails when the build or the generated environment reference has drifted. The docs pages wear the front page's key shop: to change their look, edit [`docs/_header.html`](https://github.com/waynestate/sesame/blob/HEAD/docs/_header.html) (the shop sign and main menu) and [`docs/theme/sesame.css`](https://github.com/waynestate/sesame/blob/HEAD/docs/theme/sesame.css) (palette, type, dark mode), then rebuild. Never edit the kit's `site/assets/docs.css` or `docs.js`; those are Squire's bytes.

Every page below is Markdown. The HTML pages send the same Markdown to a client that asks for `text/markdown`. Written by Squire's agent-ready kit from the README and the pages; do not edit.

## Pages

- [SESAME: The way in.](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/index.md): SESAME is Wayne State's sign-in library for PHP. It checks who someone is through CAS, OpenID Connect, an OAuth2 token or the Drawbridge gateway, and hands your app a verified identity. Your app keeps its own session. It works in raw PHP, Laravel with Blade, and Laravel with Inertia and Vue.
- [Changelog | SESAME docs](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.md): All notable changes to this project.
- [The cas driver | SESAME docs](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/driver-cas.md): Sign in against a CAS server, CAS 2.0 against Academica by default, with no per-app Entra registration.
- [The gateway driver | SESAME docs](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/driver-gateway.md): The recommended path on Citadel: verify the signed JWT assertion the Drawbridge gateway sends in one header, never a bare identity header.
- [oauth2 with Entra | SESAME docs](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/driver-oauth2-entra.md): Sign in from a JWT bearer token verified against the issuer's key set, or from an opaque token through RFC 7662 introspection, Microsoft Entra ID first, APIs only.
- [The oidc driver (Entra sign-in) | SESAME docs](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/driver-oidc.md): Browser sign-in with OpenID Connect (code flow with PKCE), Microsoft Entra ID first, for apps off Citadel and APIs.
- [The saml driver (SAML 2.0 sign-in) | SESAME docs](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/driver-saml.md): Browser sign-in as a SAML 2.0 service provider against a Shibboleth-style IdP, opt-in, with signed assertions required.
- [Strongly recommended: a git.wayne.edu instance runner | SESAME docs](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/instance-runner.md): CI for this repo runs on git.wayne.edu, on the instance runner, and every product in the stack strongly recommends the same for apps on git.wayne.edu.
- [Laravel | SESAME docs](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/laravel.md): The Laravel adapter binds the core into the container, registers the middleware aliases and the login and logout routes, and holds no rules of its own.
- [Moving from wayne-cas | SESAME docs](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/moving-from-wayne-cas.md): Apps that use wayne-cas can move to SESAME without rewriting their auth, through Booster's cas-to-sesame hop or by hand.
- [Moving off Wayne Auth | SESAME docs](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/moving-off-wayne-auth.md): Apps that sign people in through the old Wayne Auth SSO cookie can move to SESAME's CAS sign-in by changing one line, through a bridge that keeps the old WayneAuth class's calls.
- [Quick start | SESAME docs](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.md): Sign a user in from scratch with the fake driver, one step at a time.
- [Raw PHP | SESAME docs](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/raw-php.md): How a framework-free PHP app starts the session, builds the Sesame facade, signs the user in, and reads the user back.
- [Requiring MFA | SESAME docs](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/requiring-mfa.md): Require proof that the user's MFA is still good, and pick what happens when the check fails: deny with 403, or send the user back to login.
- [Running off Citadel | SESAME docs](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/running-off-citadel.md): SESAME takes its config from the app and has no platform address in code, so a move to another host is a config change, not a code change.
- [Session timeouts | SESAME docs](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/session-timeouts.md): Every signed-in session has two clocks: an idle timeout that drops it after quiet time and an absolute lifetime that ends it no matter how active it is.
- [Single-page apps | SESAME docs](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/single-page-apps.md): A single-page app reads a JSON answer to see who is signed in: sesame_status() in raw PHP and GET /sesame/status in Laravel, 200 with the session facts or 401 when signed out, never cacheable.
- [Step-up (authentication context) | SESAME docs](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/step-up.md): Send the user back through a stronger sign-in mid-session, with the prompt, max_age, acr_values and claims parameters a step-up request adds.
- [Which driver for my app? | SESAME docs](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/which-driver.md): A table that matches your situation to a driver and tells you the Entra registration it needs.
- [WSU values (Playbook) | SESAME docs](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/wsu-values.md): Four settings carry Wayne State's shared values: where the CAS server lives, and who signs the gateway and oauth2 assertions.
- [Overview | SESAME docs](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/index.md): Wayne State's protocol-neutral auth library: it returns a verified identity and leaves the session to the app.
- [Install | SESAME docs](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.md): What SESAME needs, the one composer line, and how to prove it took.
- [The oidc driver's library choice | SESAME docs](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/oidc-library-choice.md): Which library the oidc driver stands on, what else was weighed, and why.
- [API | SESAME docs](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/api.md): The classes and global functions an app uses: Config, DriverFactory, Sesame, the session, the resolver, and the sesame_* functions.
- [Configuration | SESAME docs](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.md): Every SESAME config key, its environment variable, its default and its meaning.
- [Drivers | SESAME docs](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/drivers.md): The full list of drivers and their status: fake, cas, gateway, saml, oauth2 and oidc.
- [Proof | SESAME docs](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.md): Proof runs against real Wayne State applications on a private site, behind a Wayne State employee sign-in.
- [Decision: the 60 second regenerate grace | SESAME docs](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/regenerate-grace.md): Why SESAME keeps the old session for 60 seconds after it regenerates the session ID, and how to turn that off.
- [The saml driver's library choice | SESAME docs](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/saml-library-choice.md): Which library the saml driver stands on, what else was weighed, why, and the version floor.
- [Troubleshooting | SESAME docs](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.md): What to try when a sign-in fails, and what the errors mean.
- [Upgrading | SESAME docs](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.md): How to move between SESAME versions.

## Prompts

- [Get started with SESAME](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/#prompt-get-started): Works out what kind of app you have and which driver it needs, then writes a plan. It changes nothing. The prompt itself is in https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/index.md.
- [SESAME in a raw PHP app](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/#prompt-raw-php): Sets up the config, the driver and a user resolver by hand, on your app's own session, with a logout that only accepts a POST. The prompt itself is in https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/index.md.
- [SESAME in a Laravel app with Blade](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/#prompt-laravel-blade): Publishes the config, writes a user resolver, puts auth.sesame on your routes and adds a sign-out form with a CSRF token. The prompt itself is in https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/index.md.
- [SESAME in a Laravel app with Inertia and Vue](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/#prompt-laravel-inertia): Uses the same adapter. Routes are guarded on the server, and Vue gets only the user fields it needs as a prop. The prompt itself is in https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/index.md.
- [Move a Laravel app from wayne-cas to SESAME](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/#prompt-wayne-cas): The shim keeps the old names, so most of the move is the mapping table. The agent lists every wayne-cas part before it swaps one. The prompt itself is in https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/index.md.
